raw_case_text:
A 31-year-old male presented to the emergency room complaining of progressive dyspnea and productive cough over the course of 4 months. He also noted decreased appetite with a 50-pound weight loss over the past 5 months. He had no significant past medical or surgical history and was not taking any medications. His family history was unremarkable. He quit smoking tobacco two months ago due to worsening respiratory status; he rarely used alcohol and never used recreational drugs. He was unmarried and in a long-term heterosexual relationship and denied multiple sexual partners. He was currently working in an automobile parts factory as a janitor. After high school he had enlisted in the army and served for four years; at that time he was stationed in Hawaii. While in Hawaii he visited a single prostitute on several occasions.
Initial vital signs revealed temperature was 99.9 F, blood pressure 128/83 mmHg, pulse 134 beats per minute, and respiratory rate 22 breaths/minute; oxygen saturation was 92% on room air. He was in moderate respiratory distress, yet was awake, alert, and cooperative. Extraocular muscles were intact; there was no nystagmus or scleral icterus. Pupils were equal, round, and reactive to light. He had thrush under his tongue and on the palate. There was no palpable lymphadenopathy. Heart rate was regular with no murmurs, rubs, or gallops by auscultation. There were no palpable thrills. He had equal chest rise bilaterally. Breath sounds were diminished throughout, with rales and dullness to percussion in the lower lung fields bilaterally. Sensory and motor examination was grossly intact.
Laboratory data revealed white blood count 13,900/mcL, hemoglobin 7.2 g/dL, platelets 370,000/mcL, sodium 131 mmol/L potassium 5.8 mmol/L, chloride 99 mmol/L, carbon dioxide 17 mmol/L, blood urea nitrogen 155 mg/dL, and serum creatinine 8.9 mg/dL. Arterial blood gases showed a pH of 7.39, pCO2 32.2 mmHg, bicarbonate 19.1 mmol/L, and pO2 74.5 mmHg on 3 L nasal cannula. Chest X-ray showed diffuse bilateral reticulonodular opacities (Figure 1). He was found to be HIV positive with CD4 count of <5 cells/cc and viral load of 1,180,000 copies. Bronchoalveolar lavage was preformed; Grocott's methenamine silver stain of the washings demonstrated Pneumocystis jiroveci (Figure 2). He received antibiotics and steroids with gradual improvement.
On hospital day 14, he became confused and acutely developed nystagmus with both a horizontal and prominent vertical component. He was also found to have ataxia with finger to nose testing and difficulty sitting up without support. Considering his immunosuppressed state, infectious and neoplastic etiologies were the primary diagnostic considerations. Lumbar puncture revealed clear CSF, normal opening pressure, and normal cell counts. Polymerase chain reactions for Epstein-Barr virus, Herpes simplex virus, cytomegalovirus, and John Cunningham (JC) virus were negative. Nontreponemal serological screening for syphilis (VDRL), toxoplasmosis antibody, and Cryptococcus antigen titers were negative. CT of the head did not show any intracranial mass, hemorrhage, or other acute findings. MRI of the brain revealed a slight increase in T2 signal within the medial aspect of thalamus bilaterally (Figure 3). After excluding infection and neoplasm, the clinical diagnosis of Wernicke's encephalopathy was made. Intravenous thiamine was administered resulting in resolution of symptoms, which confirmed the diagnosis.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 31-year-old male presented to the emergency department with a 4-month history of progressive dyspnea and productive cough and a 5-month history of anorexia and a 50-pound weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Previously healthy and taking no medications, the patient developed decreased appetite and a 50-pound unintentional weight loss over 5 months, accompanied for the past 4 months by progressive shortness of breath and a productive cough that prompted him to quit smoking 2 months prior to presentation.
subjective.past_medical_history: No prior known medical or surgical history. Social history: Factory janitor; former U.S. Army soldier stationed in Hawaii for 4 years (where he visited a female commercial sex worker on several occasions); currently unmarried in a long-term heterosexual relationship; quit smoking tobacco 2 months prior; rare alcohol use and no illicit drug use. Family history unremarkable.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for progressive dyspnea, productive cough, anorexia, 50-pound weight loss, and oral thrush; on hospital day 14, developed acute confusion, horizontal and vertical nystagmus, and truncal/appendicular ataxia. Taking no home medications.

objective.physical_examination: Admission vital signs: Temperature 99.9 °F, blood pressure 128/83 mmHg, pulse 134 beats/min, respiratory rate 22 breaths/min, and SpO2 92% on room air. Admission physical exam: Awake, alert, cooperative, in moderate respiratory distress; intact extraocular movements without baseline nystagmus or scleral icterus; oral candidiasis (thrush) under the tongue and on the palate; no palpable lymphadenopathy; regular tachycardia without murmurs; diminished breath sounds throughout with bibasilar rales and dullness to percussion; intact baseline motor and sensory exam. Hospital day 14 neurological exam: Acute confusion, prominent horizontal and vertical nystagmus, dysmetria/ataxia on finger-to-nose testing, and truncal ataxia (inability to sit up unsupported).
objective.routine_investigations: Admission laboratory tests: WBC 13,900/μL, hemoglobin 7.2 g/dL, platelets 370,000/μL, sodium 131 mmol/L, potassium 5.8 mmol/L, chloride 99 mmol/L, bicarbonate/CO2 17 mmol/L, BUN 155 mg/dL, and serum creatinine 8.9 mg/dL. Arterial blood gas (on 3 L/min nasal cannula): pH 7.39, pCO2 32.2 mmHg, PaO2 74.5 mmHg, HCO3- 19.1 mmol/L. HIV testing: HIV-positive with plasma HIV viral load 1,180,000 copies/mL. Admission chest X-ray: Diffuse bilateral reticulonodular opacities. Day 14 lumbar puncture and CSF analysis: Clear CSF with normal opening pressure and cell counts; negative CSF PCRs for EBV, HSV, CMV, and JC virus; negative VDRL, Toxoplasma antibody, and Cryptococcus antigen titers.
objective.advanced_workup: Baseline CD4+ T-cell count: <5 cells/mm3. Bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL): Grocott's methenamine silver (GMS) stain of BAL washings demonstrated Pneumocystis jirovecii organisms. Hospital day 14 neuroimaging: Non-contrast head CT negative for mass or hemorrhage; brain MRI demonstrated bilateral symmetrical increased T2 signal intensity within the medial thalami.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Newly diagnosed advanced HIV/AIDS (CD4 <5 cells/mm3, HIV viral load 1,180,000 copies/mL) presenting with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (confirmed by BAL Grocott's methenamine silver stain), oral candidiasis, and severe acute/chronic renal failure (creatinine 8.9 mg/dL), subsequently complicated on hospital day 14 by non-alcoholic Wernicke's encephalopathy (confirmed by classic triad of confusion, vertical/horizontal nystagmus, and ataxia, bilateral medial thalamic T2 hyperintensity on brain MRI, negative CNS opportunistic infection workup, and rapid reversal with thiamine). Plan and clinical course: Treated with targeted anti-Pneumocystis antibiotics and adjunctive corticosteroids with gradual respiratory improvement; on hospital day 14, administration of intravenous thiamine resulted in rapid resolution of his confusion, nystagmus, and ataxia.
